title: FedEx Supports Climate Resilience in Northern Vietnam Through Mangrove Planting
summary: FedEx team members join local partners to support coastal ecosystems and community resilience in Thai Thuy, Hung Yen Province
body_markdown:
Federal Express Corporation (FedEx), one of the world’s largest express transportation companies, joined local partners to support climate resilience efforts in northern Vietnam through a mangrove planting activity at Thai Thuy Wetland Nature Reserve in Thai Thuy Commune, Hung Yen Province.


The initiative, part of the Environmental Ambassadors 2026 project, brought together 40 FedEx volunteers and representatives from MSD United Way Vietnam, alongside Thai Thuy Centre for Clean Water, Agricultural Engineering and Nature Conservation. Together, they planted 200 mangrove trees, locally known as bần chua, with guidance from technical staff. Their contribution was part of the project’s overall objective of planting 2,000 mangrove trees along the sea dike across one hectare at the reserve.


The planting site lies within Thai Thuy Wetland Nature Reserve, a coastal wetland area important for local ecosystems and biodiversity. The coastal region faces climate-related challenges, including erosion, saline intrusion, flooding and extreme weather. Mangroves can help reduce wave energy and coastal erosion, provide habitats for wildlife and support livelihoods connected to aquaculture and coastal agriculture. Realizing these benefits, however, depends on suitable planting practices, successful establishment and continued care. Following planting, the one-hectare mangrove area will be cared for, maintained and monitored for three years by MSD United Way Vietnam in coordination with the Thai Thuy Centre for Clean Water, Agricultural Engineering and Nature Conservation and technical partners, before being handed over to local authorities for continued management and protection.


FedEx’s participation marks its second hands-on environmental conservation initiative in collaboration with MSD United Way Vietnam, following their mangrove restoration activity in Vinh Long earlier in 2026. This contribution is part of FedEx Cares’ Planting for Good efforts and reflects the company’s values to support communities and engage team members around the world in hands-on conservation efforts.


“Local environmental action is most meaningful when it responds to the needs of the communities where we operate,” said Ee-Hui Tan, managing director, FedEx Vietnam and Cambodia. “By bringing our team members together with local partners in Thai Thuy, we are supporting the protection of a coastal ecosystem that is important to local livelihoods and biodiversity. These collaborations are an important part of how we put our commitment to supporting communities into action.”


“Planting trees in a mangrove area helps each of us better understand the connection between nature and the lives of coastal communities. Through the Environmental Ambassadors project, MSD hopes that every volunteer and every business will become an ambassador: drawing on their experience to share the story of mangroves, inspire others and encourage more people to protect and restore them. MSD is committed to continuing to connect and work with local organizations so that today’s experiences lead to lasting action,” said Le Anh Ngoc, Director of MSD United Way Vietnam.


The activity builds on FedEx Cares’ broader environmental efforts in Vietnam, which include urban tree planting in Ho Chi Minh City and mangrove restoration in Vinh Long earlier in 2026. Through collaboration with local organizations and employee volunteering, FedEx aims to contribute to practical environmental initiatives that support the communities where its team members live and work. Before planting, FedEx volunteers received technical guidance and learned about the role of mangroves in coastal protection and local livelihoods. The project encourages participants to share these experiences with colleagues, families and their communities, inspiring further action to protect nature.
